title: MQSS-Selector: RL-Guided Pass Selection for an MLIR Compilation Pipeline
authors: Andre Youssefi, Ercüment Kaya, Minh Chung, Jorge Echavarria, Laura B. Schulz, Martin Schulz
abstract: High Performance Computing (HPC) and Quantum Computing (QC) systems are increasingly converging towards unified High Performance Computing-Quantum Computing (HPCQC) infrastructures, driven by a growing need to bridge classical and quantum workflows, which affects all levels of the system stack, from the hardware to compilers and runtimes, all the way to applications. However, today's QC devices are still in the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era, are error-prone and resource-limited, and therefore require specialized optimizations and topology mappings to achieve sufficient fidelity. This places special emphasis on proper compilation and optimization within the overall quantum software stack. Many existing stacks remain fragmented, with separate components responsible for device selection, compiler-pass optimization, and job queue scheduling. This paper proposes a unified, learning-based selector that integrates these disparate stages into a cohesive framework. Our proposed selector scheme leverages reinforcement learning and deep learning models that can be extended to simultaneously optimize multiple objectives -- such as fidelity, compilation time, and scheduling latency -- while dynamically adapting to circuit characteristics and device conditions.
summary: This paper introduces MQSS-Selector, a novel reinforcement learning framework designed to solve the complex problem of quantum program compilation. It unifies device selection and compiler pass optimization into a single scheduler to maximize performance metrics like fidelity and minimize latency. This is crucial for bridging classical HPC resources with error-prone quantum hardware in the NISQ era.
main_problem: The challenge of optimizing quantum program compilation by jointly selecting the best quantum device and the optimal sequence of compiler optimization passes.
main_result: The authors propose MQSS-Selector, an RL-guided framework that unifies device selection and pass ordering to optimize multiple objectives simultaneously.
method: They leverage Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents interacting with a simulated quantum software stack environment to learn optimal scheduling policies.
model_or_system: The system targets High Performance Computing-Quantum Computing (HPCQC) infrastructures operating in the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era, dealing with quantum circuits and compilation pipelines.
key_observables: Fidelity (Hellinger fidelity), compilation time, scheduling latency, program depth, and operation count.
important_parameters: Device topology, gate fidelity, queueing delay, and the set of available compiler passes.
main_assumptions: The joint optimization problem is shown to be NP-hard, necessitating heuristic/approximation algorithms like RL.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the integrated scheduling pipeline combining device selection and phase ordering optimization for quantum program execution.
paper_structure: The paper frames the problem as a Design Space Exploration (DSE) and proposes a unified RL selector, detailing components for device selection (using supervised ML) and pass ordering (using RL).
why_interesting: It addresses the critical software stack challenges in realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation by providing a learning-based optimization layer for resource-constrained NISQ devices.

Fig. 4 shows the results on the MQT dataset. It displays the model’s fidelity predictions for the 128 MQT-bench programs on the chosen twelve backends. The results show a worse performance by MLP, compared to the other models. We expect fine tuning to improve the predictions. While SVM and KNN show good results for fidelity predictions, they may not be a fitting choice for algorithms in the unified scheduler. Their good performance is based on the limited data set.
